body.p: A hare and a wolverine. A hare ran along a road. An old wolverine ran towards him. "Where did you come from, hare?[ShA:] Normally, kuniz (ABL) should be "I walked off-road for several days. My legs hurt, my head hurts, I have no strength.here, not LOC.[ShA:] Normally, I would expect nixu-jq, e.g. lit. my force. I am going back." The wolverine said: "Don't go. If you go back, you'll fall into a trap [ShA:] N'iz is completely unexpected as the 2sg imperative form; typically,the expected future form is kan(u)t (irregular).on the road. Surely, a man has already installed a trap. Don't go back, go forward. If you go along a new road, you will find something, you will not be killed, you will not fall into a trap."[ShA:] Normall, not n'iz, but n'id' is the expected form of 2sg.md. Their roads diverged in different directions. The hare did not follow the advice and went back. He thought that he had not obeyed the old wolverine before and had lived well. "Why should she teach me now?"[ShA:] Normally, tÉxo is intransitive.He went back. In the evening, Wolverine goes home. "Oh, what is lying there?" The hare lies across the [ShA:] No no is attested road, eyes closed, mouth open. He died, he became completely cold.anywhere for open. He fell into a trap. Only his ears are visible. The wolverine feels sorry for the hare.[ShA:] The syntax is completely unexpected and presumably follows Russian pattern.
